text:
amanda: Starting TF apply for release/2026-03-20 in the midday change window. Plan looked clean; canary gated. I'm going to kick off in ~5m. @samir @laura please ack and watch metrics.

deploybot: Deploy started: terraform apply —target=module/network —auto-approve 
```
Apply: 13 added, 2 changed, 1 destroyed
Resources: 16 added, 2 changed, 1 destroyed
Outputs: none
Plan time: 00:02:14
```

samir: ack. i'll watch infra metrics (net/iam) and traffic routing. will flag 502/504 or >10% 99th latency regression.

laura: watching logs and rollout trace. @kevin are you on-call for iam fallout?

kevin: yep I'm on it. I see we're pinning provider to hashicorp/aws v4.2.0 in the plan — double-checking the sa binding change.

maria: release notes: <https://docs.internal/releases/2026-03-20|release-2026-03-20> — includes network egress rewrite and a small IAM change for inference-service-sa.

infra-sre-bot: Metric alert: us-east-1 inference-pool latency p99 increased 18% at 12:37:42 UTC :eyes:

deploybot: Auto-pause triggered (latency threshold breached). Apply paused at step 7/16.

amanda: holding. good catch. samir can you surface which resource caused the spike?

samir: looks correlated with aws_lb_target_group_attachment change for inference-green-targets. health checks returned more 503s as we shifted 10% traffic.

laura: we ran canary at 10% traffic by design. are the health checks too strict? I can relax timeout in ASG for 2 minutes to let backends settle.

kevin: IAM change is minimal (add GetObject on s3 bucket) — not likely the cause. Reverting network step would be fastest rollback. Deploybot, can you show pending step ids?

'terraform-plan-bot: Pending steps: step_7: aws_lb_target_group_attachment.update[3] (inference), step_8: aws_lb_target_group_attachment.add[5], step_9: aws_lb_listener_rule.priority_shift

amanda: two options: 1) abort and rollback to commit abcdef1 (fastest), or 2) resume after relaxing health check and shift traffic slower (10% -> 25% -> 50%). Thoughts?

samir: prefer option 2 if we can step traffic slower and keep apply paused for 10m. If any more 5xx we rollback.

kevin: agree with controlled roll forward. add an escape hatch: if p50 latency > 250ms or error rate > 3% for 5m, we stop and revert.

maria: ops checklist updated with note about rollback commits and terraform state snapshot: snapshot: s3://tfstate/releases/2026-03-20/snap-3055551200.

deploybot: Resume requested by amanda. Resuming apply in gated mode: traffic-shift-step=10%.

amanda: doing manual traffic shift scheduler: 10% -> 25% in 5m -> 50% in 10m. samir and laura pls ack when stable.

infra-sre-bot: Watch window started. Monitoring p50/p99, 5xx count, LB unhealthy hosts.

laura: 5m mark — p99 dropped to +5% vs baseline, 5xx stayed flat. moving to 25%.

samir: 25% hold, healthy hosts stable. no new errors. moving to 50% now.

kevin: IAM post-checks look good. no permission denies observed.

maria: adding note to release notes: "Network canary was gated; rolled forward after health check tuning; no customer impact observed."

amanda: apply finished fully at 12:52 UTC. final state shows 16/16 resources applied. Good job everyone.

deploybot: Apply complete. Terraform state uploaded: s3://tfstate/releases/2026-03-20/terraform.tfstate. Commit linked: abcdef1 -> release/2026-03-20

kevin: one follow-up: create a quick unit-test for lb healthcheck tolerance in staging to avoid this in future.

samir: filing ticket: INFRA-1229 — "Increase LB healthcheck stabilization tolerance for inference pool canaries"

laura: closing watch. thanks all. :tada:
